subject: chemistry
question_text: Define threshold frequency and work function.

verification.note: PREDICTED, not asked. Both the question and the 1+1 mark split are claims until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms them. AI chemistry check 2026-08-25: W₀ = hν₀ and both definitions verified; one common mistake reworded to say that intensity does not give each photon more energy, in place of not making it stronger (explanation text only, marked lines and marks untouched).

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Threshold frequency
lines: frequency of light needed to eject an
Below ν₀ no electron is ejected.
steps.why: One photon frees one electron, so the photon must carry at least enough energy on its own. The frequency at which it carries exactly enough is the threshold frequency, and it is different for every metal.
common_mistakes: Saying it is the minimum intensity. Intensity sends more photons, it does not give each one more energy.
steps.memory_tip: Threshold is the lowest frequency that works. Below it, nothing happens at all.
steps.margin_note: Write the symbol ν₀ with the definition.

steps.label: Work function
lines: It is the minimum energy needed to remove
an electron from the metal surface.
Alkali metals have a low work function.
steps.why: The work function is the same idea as the threshold frequency, measured in energy instead of frequency, and h is what converts one into the other. A low work function is why the alkali metals show the photoelectric effect most readily.
common_mistakes: Writing W₀ = hν, using the frequency of the incoming light instead of the threshold frequency.
Giving the work function a unit of frequency. It is an energy.
steps.memory_tip: Threshold is measured in frequency, work function in energy. Multiply by h to move between them.
steps.margin_note: W₀ = hν₀ links the two halves of this answer in one line.

insider_note: Two definitions, one mark each, and each is a single line. W₀ = hν₀ links them and is worth adding even though the question asks only for the definitions.
